reviewProfile: UX implementation, browser assertions and direct visual inspection
scope: Correction of observed UI blockers on the existing portal; no new shell, navigation section or business metric.
implementation: Current open questions appear as an explicit list at the end of the chat, independent of the consulted message page and including when a proposal already exists. The action focuses the composer without overwriting its draft.

Failed/nonvalidated chat output remains stored but is collapsed as nonvalidated evidence instead of appearing as a normal reply. Recovery uses the original message and preserves uncertainty about actual business effects.

Blocked preparation with no external-effect marker offers reviewed resume of the same intent via the existing endpoint, preserving original source/version. A nonexistent effect is not offered for reconciliation. Operations with actual effect/uncertainty retain reconciliation.
Preparation presents a concrete next step and preserves actor, version, recovery, reason and evidence; wording is generic to the System instead of referring to courses/orders.

Dependency consent is requested only with a prepared decision and explains that it concerns software libraries/packages. A preliminary conversation does not demand consent; the user is told to ask for necessity and impact if not explicit.
DEV states the dependency on the current revision merge before construction/publication and provides the sequence of subsequent controls without asserting execution or deployment.

contractAlignment.resumeContract: Same /resume endpoint, expectedVersion and confirmed; backend must revalidate before any effect. Blocked with no write marker is now allowed alongside paused.

tests.qualification: Isolated portal_test with HTTP-intercepted scenarios. Validates UI behavior/recovery and does not attest real agents, GitLab, image build or DEV deployment.

previousAttempt.result: Stopped before browser tests because catalog needed update. No failed browser scenario was hidden.

limitations: Publication and end-to-end jewelry acceptance belong to the parent real-browser journey.
UI change does not repair executor/profile or context-budget defects by itself.
Does not certify complete accessibility, all browsers or the whole portal.
Does not rewrite failed outputs, agent results, old audit or business data.
Does not create new approval or automatic software dependency authorization.
